::: {.page-intro}
I develop software that connects flood research with repeatable analysis and engineering practice.
My work spans Python, PyTorch, GDAL, and QGIS.
:::

## Research software

::: {.software-grid}
::: {.software-item}
[SUPER-RESOLUTION]{.software-category}

### floodSR

AI super-resolution of flood hazard rasters using low-resolution inundation grids and high-resolution digital elevation models.

**Role:** Lead developer · **Stack:** Python, PyTorch, GDAL

[Repository →](https://github.com/cefect/floodsr)
:::

::: {.software-item}
[DOWNSCALING]{.software-category}

### FloodDownscaler2

Flood-grid downscaling with CostGrow resampling, least-cost mapping, and high-and-dry filtering.

**Role:** Lead developer · **Stack:** Python, WhiteboxTools

[Repository →](https://github.com/cefect/FloodDownscaler2)
:::

::: {.software-item}
[FLOOD-DEPTH ESTIMATION]{.software-category}

### RICorDE

Gridded water-depth estimation from flood inundation using height above nearest drainage (HAND) and cost-distance extrapolation.

**Role:** Lead developer · **Stack:** PyQGIS, WhiteboxTools

[Repository →](https://github.com/NRCan/RICorDE) · [Methods paper](https://doi.org/10.5194/nhess-22-1437-2022)
:::

::: {.software-item}
[RISK MODELLING]{.software-category}

### CanFlood / CanFlood2

QGIS tools for flood-risk modelling, sensitivity analysis, multi-model workflows, and reporting.

**Role:** Lead developer · **Stack:** Python, QGIS

[CanFlood](https://github.com/NRCan/CanFlood) · [CanFlood2 →](https://github.com/cefect/CanFlood2)
:::

::: {.software-item}
[VULNERABILITY]{.software-category}

### CanCurve

A QGIS plugin for creating Canadian flood depth-damage functions, with SQLite-backed project data and CanFlood-format exports.

**Role:** Lead developer · **Stack:** Python, QGIS, SQLite

[Repository →](https://github.com/NRCan/CanCurve)
:::
:::

## Data and reproducibility

For data supporting published studies, follow the data-availability statements in the [papers](publications.qmd).
Software documentation, installation requirements, citation instructions, and license terms are maintained in each repository.

USFloods is ongoing research; a public dataset release is not listed here yet.
